questions.question: How should pre-trip inspections be done?

options.text: Differently each time to check different items.
The same way each time so you don't forget anything.

questions.correctAnswerText: The same way each time so you don't forget anything.
questions.explanation: Do the same pre-trip inspection before every drive. This routine helps you remember all steps and prevents you from missing anything.

questions.question: If shipping papers say "Inhalation Hazard," what must you do?

options.text: Use an inhalation hazard placard only if you transport more than 100 pounds.
Use an inhalation hazard placard for any amount of the material.
Give air masks to anyone handling the cargo.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use an inhalation hazard placard for any amount of the material.
questions.explanation: If shipping papers say "Inhalation Hazard," you must display the correct inhalation hazard placards along with any other required placards. This applies no matter how much material you are carrying.

questions.question: What does a material's hazard class show?

options.text: How fast the material must get to its destination.

questions.explanation: Hazardous materials are placed into one of nine classes. Each class explains what type of danger the material poses.

questions.question: What is the correct way to do an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back up to the left.
Back up straight, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back up straight.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back up to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must be completely inside the parking space boundaries.

questions.question: Which incident does NOT require a National Response Center notification?

options.text: Injury that does not need hospitalization.

questions.correctAnswerText: Injury that does not need hospitalization.
questions.explanation: You must notify the National Response Center for: death, hospitalization, $50,000 or more in property damage, public evacuation, closure of major routes for more than one hour, or fire and spillage involving hazardous materials. You must also report if you think the situation is serious enough.

questions.question: How should a shipper warn others about hazardous materials?

options.text: Put HazMat placards on the truck.
Put flashing lights on the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: Put HazMat placards on the truck.
questions.explanation: Shippers of hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs, called placards, on vehicles. Shippers must provide placards, labels, shipping papers, and emergency information.

questions.question: Where must a hazardous materials placard be placed?

options.text: On the outside of the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the outside of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Hazardous materials placards must be placed on the front, rear, and both sides of the vehicle.

questions.question: In a vehicle control skills test, what is a "look"?

options.text: Checking the gauges on your instrument panel.
Getting out and walking to the back of your vehicle to check its position.

questions.correctAnswerText: Getting out and walking to the back of your vehicle to check its position.
questions.explanation: A look is when you open your door, get out, and walk to the back of the vehicle to check where it is. During straight line backing, you may only use one look. During other exercises, you may use up to two looks.

questions.question: If your vehicle carrying explosives breaks down, how should you warn other drivers?

options.text: By standing on the road and waving your arms.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle breaks down while carrying explosives, use reflective triangles or red electric lights for warning signals. Never use burning signals like flares or fuses with explosives.

questions.question: What shape is a hazardous materials placard?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: What does a shipping paper describe?

options.text: How the materials will be transported
Who should accept the materials being transported

questions.explanation: Shipping papers must describe the specific hazardous materials being transported.

questions.question: If you notice a cargo leak, how should you identify the leaking hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: If cargo leaks, use the shipping papers, label, or package location to identify the materials. Do not touch or smell leaking materials — this could cause serious injury or death.

questions.question: What is used to warn others of hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: Diamond-shaped signs called placards are placed on bulk packages and vehicles to warn others of hazardous materials. The shipper must place the placards, and the driver must verify they are correct.

questions.question: To complete a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest, you must:

options.text: Only sign the manifest if you cross into another state.
Have a witness sign the manifest.

questions.explanation: When transporting hazardous waste, you must carry a Uniform Hazardous Waste Manifest. The manifest must be signed by hand.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, you may be asked to:

options.text: Drive straight into a parking space.

questions.explanation: The basic vehicle control skills test may include straight line backing, offset back/right parking, offset back/left parking, driver side parallel parking, conventional parallel parking, and alley docking.

questions.question: The power unit of a placarded vehicle must carry a fire extinguisher with a minimum rating of:
questions.explanation: A placarded vehicle's power unit must have a fire extinguisher with a UL rating of 10 B:C or higher.

questions.question: Placards must be placed:

options.text: Within three inches of other markings.
So words or numbers are read from left to right.

questions.correctAnswerText: So words or numbers are read from left to right.
questions.explanation: Placards must be placed at least three inches away from other markings. Words and numbers must be level and read from left to right.

questions.question: If corrosive materials leak in a trailer, the trailer should be:

options.text: Left to air dry without washing.

questions.explanation: Parts of a vehicle exposed to corrosive liquids must be thoroughly washed with water.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, the liquid discharge valves should be:
questions.explanation: Liquid discharge valves on compressed gas tanks must be closed except when loading and unloading.

questions.question: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on a shipping paper, which placard should the shipper provide?

options.text: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard

questions.correctAnswerText: Poison Gas or Poison Inhalation Hazard
questions.explanation: If "Inhalation Hazard" appears on the shipping paper or package, display the "Poison Inhalation Hazard" or "Poison Gas" placard as appropriate.

questions.question: When loading compressed gas, should the liquid discharge valves be open or closed?
questions.explanation: Liquid discharge valves must be opened during loading and unloading. At all other times, keep them closed.

questions.question: What will the examiner score you on during the driving test?

options.text: How quickly you arrive at your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving maneuvers and general driving behavior. You must drive safely and responsibly. Obey all traffic signs, signals, and laws. Do not cause an accident or commit a moving violation.

questions.question: If your driving test route does not include a railroad crossing, what will happen?

options.text: You will not have to do anything related to railroad crossings.
You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
You will have to take the test again on a route with a railroad crossing.

questions.correctAnswerText: You may have to explain how you would cross railroad tracks.
questions.explanation: If your route does not include a railroad crossing, the examiner may ask you to explain and show how you would properly cross railroad tracks at a simulated location.

questions.question: When asked to make a turn during your driving test, what should you do?

options.text: Use your turn signal only if other cars are present.
Check traffic only in the direction you are turning.

questions.explanation: When making a turn, check traffic in all directions and always use your turn signal.

questions.question: What shape are hazardous material warning signs on vehicles?
questions.explanation: Vehicles carrying hazardous materials must display diamond-shaped warning signs on all four sides. These signs are called placards.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT your job as a driver at an accident scene?

options.text: Keeping people away from the scene.
Trying to fight hazardous materials fires.
Telling emergency responders about the hazardous materials.

questions.correctAnswerText: Trying to fight hazardous materials fires.
questions.explanation: Your responsibilities at an accident scene are: keep people away, limit material spread if safe, inform emergency responders of dangers, and provide shipping papers. Do not try to fight hazardous materials fires unless you have protective equipment and proper training.

questions.question: Who is responsible for properly labeling hazardous materials?
questions.explanation: The shipper is responsible for packaging, marking, and labeling hazardous materials correctly. The driver should verify the materials are properly labeled.

questions.question: What is the first step when alley docking?

options.text: Position your vehicle directly in front of the alley.
Back up directly in front of the alley.
Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop parallel to the outer boundary of the alley.
questions.explanation: First, pull past the alley and stop parallel to its outer boundary. Then back your vehicle straight into the alley parking space, keeping it within the boundaries.

questions.question: How do you complete an offset back/right parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then back to the right.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the right.
questions.explanation: First pull straight forward, then back up to the right. Park your vehicle completely within the space boundaries.

questions.question: What should you do when asked to change lanes during the driving test?

options.text: Do not be concerned with other motorists.
Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
Change lanes as quickly as possible, even if it means cutting off another driver.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use your turn signal and change lanes when safe.
questions.explanation: Check traffic, use your turn signal, and smoothly change lanes only when it is safe to do so.
